note: Gap-fill for gym_exercises.json (free-exercise-db, 882 entries, ~2010s bodybuilding.com-era). Two kinds of entry. `exercises` are movements with no equivalent in the source dataset under any name -- modern machines (pendulum/belt squat, hip thrust and lateral raise machines), the cable-isolation and chest-supported-row vocabulary, glute-specific work, and conditioning. They carry `images: []` because free-exercise-db is the only public-domain source of the paired start/end ROM photos the catalog uses, and it has no counterpart for them; the UI falls back to the muscle map. `aliases` are names people actually search for that map onto a row that ALREADY exists -- no new row, no new images needed.
source: Gaps identified by diffing the catalog against StrengthLog's most-trained-exercise rankings and exercise directory, and Jeff Nippard's per-muscle tier lists.

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat
instructions: Set the shoulder pads so they rest on your traps with your knees slightly bent, and place your feet flat on the platform about shoulder-width apart.
Release the safety handles and let the arc of the machine carry you down until your thighs pass parallel.
Drive through the whole foot to return to the start without locking the knees out hard.
Because the machine supports your torso, the lower back is largely taken out of the lift -- push the quads closer to failure than you would on a barbell squat.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
instructions: Fasten the belt around your hips and stand on the platform with feet shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the load and squat down under control, keeping your torso tall.
Drive back up through the midfoot to full hip extension.
The load hangs from the hips rather than the spine, so this is the go-to squat pattern when back or shoulder issues limit bar work.

exercises.name: Vertical Leg Press
instructions: Lie on your back under the machine and place your feet flat on the platform directly above your hips.
Release the safeties and lower the platform until your knees reach roughly 90 degrees.
Press straight up through the whole foot without letting your hips roll off the pad.
Keep your lower back flat against the pad throughout -- the vertical angle makes it easy to tuck the pelvis at the bottom.

exercises.name: Front Foot Elevated Split Squat
instructions: Place your front foot on a low plate or step and take a split stance, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Lower until the back knee is just off the floor, keeping most of your weight on the front leg.
Drive up through the front heel.
Elevating the front foot deepens hip flexion, which biases the glute more than a flat-footed split squat.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
instructions: Kneel upright on a pad with your knees hip-width apart and your glutes squeezed.
Keeping a straight line from knee to shoulder, lean backwards under control as far as you can.
Pull yourself back upright using the quads.
Loads the quads in a deeply stretched position, which is why it is one of the few effective quad exercises needing no equipment.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
instructions: Set the safety squat bar across your traps and grip the handles in front of your shoulders.
Unrack, step back, and squat to depth keeping your chest up -- the cambered bar will push you forward if you let it.
Drive back up through the midfoot.
The neutral handle position removes the shoulder external rotation a straight bar demands, so it suits lifters with shoulder or elbow restrictions.

exercises.name: Landmine Squat
instructions: Hold the end of a landmine-mounted barbell at chest height with both hands.
Squat down, letting the bar's arc pull you into a slightly forward-leaning but upright torso position.
Drive back up through the heels.
The bar path acts as a counterweight, which makes this a good way to teach depth to lifters who fold forward under a back squat.

exercises.name: Pause Squat
instructions: Set up and descend as you would for a back squat.
Hold the bottom position for two to three seconds without relaxing or letting the chest drop.
Drive up out of the hole with no bounce.
Removing the stretch reflex exposes weakness out of the bottom, so expect to use noticeably less load than a touch-and-go squat.

exercises.name: Pin Squat
instructions: Set the rack pins at the height you want to work from.
Squat down until the bar rests fully on the pins and let the load settle.
Re-brace and drive the bar off the pins from a dead stop.
Starting from zero momentum makes this the most specific way to train a sticking point at a given height.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet much wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight over one leg and sink into a deep squat on that side, letting the other leg straighten with the toes up.
Push back to the centre and repeat on the other side.
Trains the adductors through a long range, which is why it doubles as a hip mobility drill.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Step one leg diagonally behind and across the other, lowering until the back knee is just off the floor.
Drive back to standing through the front heel.
The crossed-over position puts the working hip into adduction, which biases the glute medius.

exercises.name: Air Squat
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms out in front for balance.
Sit back and down until the hips drop below the knees.
Stand back up to full hip extension.
The default unloaded squat used for warm-ups and conditioning circuits.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
instructions: Stand with a wide stance and toes turned out roughly 45 degrees, holding one dumbbell between your legs.
Squat straight down, keeping the knees tracking over the toes.
Drive up through the heels, squeezing the glutes at the top.
The wide stance shifts emphasis onto the adductors and glutes relative to a conventional squat.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pad across your hips and your back against the support.
Drive your hips forward until they are fully extended and your shins are vertical.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top, then lower under control.
Removes the barbell setup friction that limits how often people actually train the hip thrust pattern.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench and rest a dumbbell across one hip.
Plant one foot and lift the other leg off the floor.
Drive the hips up through the planted heel to full extension, then lower under control.
Keep the hips level -- letting the free side drop turns this into a lateral stability exercise instead.

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through
instructions: Set a rope attachment at the lowest pulley position and face away from the stack, straddling the cable.
Hinge at the hips, letting the rope travel back between your legs while keeping a flat back.
Stand tall by driving the hips forward, squeezing the glutes at the top.
The cable pulls horizontally, so resistance peaks at lockout -- the opposite of a Romanian deadlift's strength curve.

exercises.name: Frog Pump
instructions: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides.
Rest a dumbbell on your hips if adding load.
Drive the hips up, squeezing the glutes hard at the top, then lower.
The externally rotated hip position keeps tension on the glutes rather than letting the quads and hamstrings take over.

exercises.name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent about 45 degrees and a band around your thighs, feet together.
Keeping your feet in contact, rotate the top knee open as far as you can without rolling your hips back.
Lower under control.
Standard glute medius activation drill -- rolling the top hip backwards is the usual cheat and removes the point of the exercise.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side.
Lower under control without letting the torso rotate.
Keep the spine still -- if the ribs twist, the hip has stopped doing the work.

exercises.name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Keeping the knee bent, drive one heel towards the ceiling until the thigh is in line with your torso.
Lower without letting the lower back arch.
Stop the lift when the hip stops extending -- extra height comes from the lumbar spine, not the glute.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place a loop band around your legs just above the knees or around the ankles.
Drop into a quarter squat and step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Take several steps in one direction, then return.
Do not let the trailing foot snap in -- controlling the return step is where most of the work happens.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip, letting the free leg travel back as a counterweight and keeping the back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
Keep the hips square to the floor -- opening them turns the lift into a rotation exercise.

exercises.name: Standing Glute Kickback Machine
instructions: Stand facing the machine with your working foot against the pad and hold the supports.
Drive the pad back by extending the hip, keeping your torso upright.
Squeeze the glute at full extension, then return under control.
Resist the urge to lean forward to gain range -- that comes from the lower back.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
instructions: Set the pad just below your hip crease and hook your heels under the rollers.
Hinge forward at the hips with a rounded or neutral spine as preferred.
Drive back up by squeezing the glutes, stopping in line with the pad rather than hyperextending.
Rounding the upper back deliberately and finishing with a hard glute squeeze biases the glutes over the spinal erectors.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
instructions: Lie chest-down on the angled pad and grip the handles with arms fully extended.
Row the handles towards your hips, driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
With the torso supported, the lower back is removed from the lift, so the upper back can be trained close to failure safely.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to roughly 30-45 degrees and lie chest-down with a dumbbell in each hand.
Row both dumbbells towards your hips, keeping your chest in contact with the pad.
Lower to a full stretch under control.
Because the bench prevents body english, load will be lower than a bent-over row -- that is the point.

exercises.name: Seal Row
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench raised high enough that the bar clears the floor at full stretch.
Row the bar to the bench, driving the elbows back.
Lower to a dead hang without letting your chest leave the bench.
The strictest row variation available -- no leg drive or hip extension can contribute.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
instructions: Set up over the bar with your torso parallel to the floor and a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Row the bar explosively to your lower chest.
Return the bar all the way to the floor and reset before each rep.
Every rep starts from a dead stop, so this builds starting strength rather than time under tension.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
instructions: Stand side-on to a landmine-mounted barbell and take a staggered stance, bracing your free hand on your thigh.
Grip the end of the bar with an overhand grip and row it up towards your hip.
Lower to a full stretch, letting the shoulder blade travel forward.
The side-on position and the bar's arc create a strong stretch at the bottom of each rep.

exercises.name: Kroc Row
instructions: Brace one hand on a bench or rack and hold a heavy dumbbell in the other.
Row for high reps, allowing controlled hip and torso english to move the weight.
Keep the lowering phase controlled and reach a full stretch each rep.
Deliberately loose compared with a strict row -- it is a high-rep grip and upper-back builder, not a form exercise.

exercises.name: Yates Row
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip and hinge to roughly 45 degrees, more upright than a bent-over row.
Row the bar to your lower abdomen, driving the elbows back and down.
Lower under control.
The upright torso allows heavier loading than a parallel-torso row at the cost of some upper-back range.

exercises.name: Gorilla Row
instructions: Stand over two kettlebells with a wide stance and hinge until you can grip both.
Row one kettlebell to your hip while the other stays on the floor as a base.
Lower it and alternate sides.
The grounded kettlebell acts as a counterweight, so this loads the working lat while heavily resisting rotation.

exercises.name: Cable Lat Prayer
instructions: Set a rope or bar at a high pulley and kneel facing the stack, arms extended overhead.
Keeping the elbows slightly bent and fixed, pull the handle down in an arc towards your thighs.
Let the arms return overhead until you feel a full lat stretch.
A straight-arm pulldown done kneeling, which removes the temptation to add body english.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Lat Pulldown
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and kneel or sit side-on to the stack.
Grip the handle with the far hand so the cable crosses in front of your body.
Pull down and across towards the opposite hip, then return to a full overhead stretch.
The diagonal path follows the lat's fibre direction, giving a longer working range than a straight pulldown.

exercises.name: Ring Row
instructions: Hang gymnastic rings at waist height and grip one in each hand, walking your feet forward to lean back.
Pull your chest to the rings, keeping a straight line from head to heels.
Lower under control to full arm extension.
Difficulty is set by foot position -- walk the feet further forward to make it harder.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
instructions: Set the bar on rack pins at or just below knee height.
Take a deadlift stance and grip, brace, and pull the bar to lockout.
Lower it back to the pins under control.
Shortening the range allows supramaximal loading of the lockout and the upper back.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set a handle at the lowest pulley and stand side-on, gripping it with the outside hand across your body.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, leading with the elbow.
Lower under control.
The cable keeps tension on the side delt at the bottom of the rep, where a dumbbell has almost none.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Adjust the seat so the pivot point lines up with your shoulder joint.
Press the pads outward and up to shoulder height.
Lower under control without letting the weight stack touch down.
The fixed path makes it easy to take side-delt work to true failure without cheating with the torso.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
instructions: Sit facing the pad and grip the handles with arms extended in front of you.
Sweep the handles out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows.
Squeeze the rear delts, then return under control.
Keep the elbows relatively high -- dropping them turns this into a row and recruits the lats.

exercises.name: Cable Y-Raise
instructions: Set two low pulleys and grip the opposite handle in each hand so the cables cross in front of you.
Raise both arms up and out into a Y position overhead.
Lower under control.
Trains the rear and side delts together with the lower traps, which most delt isolation misses.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set a handle at the lowest pulley and stand so the cable runs behind your back.
Grip the handle with the outside hand and raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Running the cable behind the body keeps the delt loaded in a slightly stretched position at the bottom.

exercises.name: Lean-In Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Hold a rack upright with one hand and lean away from it so your body is angled.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand and raise it out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Leaning increases the moment arm at the bottom of the rep, loading the stretched position a standing raise cannot.

exercises.name: Viking Press
instructions: Stand inside the Viking press handles and grip them at shoulder height with a neutral grip.
Press overhead until the arms lock out, letting the arc of the machine guide the bar path.
Lower under control to shoulder height.
The neutral grip and fixed arc are easier on the shoulders than a straight-bar overhead press.

exercises.name: Landmine Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand side-on to a landmine-mounted barbell and grip the end with the far hand.
Raise the bar out and across to shoulder height, following the bar's arc.
Lower under control.
The arc loads the side delt hardest near the top, unlike a dumbbell raise which peaks at horizontal.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Press the handles forward until your arms are extended without locking out hard.
Return under control to a full stretch.
The stable path lets you push to failure without a spotter, which is why it is a staple hypertrophy press.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Chest Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit just below your collarbones.
Press up and forward until the arms are extended.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
Biases the upper chest while keeping the stability benefits of a fixed path.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Chest Fly
instructions: Sit on a bench between two pulleys set at roughly shoulder height, a handle in each hand.
With a slight fixed bend in the elbows, bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Return under control until you feel a full stretch across the chest.
Sitting removes the balance demand of a standing crossover, keeping the chest under constant tension.

exercises.name: Cable Press-Around
instructions: Set a single handle at roughly chest height and stand side-on with the cable behind you.
Grip the handle with the near hand and press it forward and across your body until the arm is extended.
Return under control to a stretched position.
A hybrid of a fly and a press that keeps tension on the inner chest through lockout.

exercises.name: Hex Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells pressed firmly together over your chest.
Keeping them squeezed together, lower to your chest.
Press back up, maintaining inward pressure throughout.
The constant adduction keeps the chest contracted at lockout, where a normal press hands off to the triceps.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
instructions: Place each hand on a low parallette, block, or dumbbell so your hands sit above floor level.
Lower your chest below hand level, keeping the body in a straight line.
Press back up to full extension.
The extra depth loads the chest in a stretched position an ordinary push-up cannot reach.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
instructions: Attach weight with a dip belt and support yourself on parallel bars at arm's length.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, leaning the torso forward to bias the chest.
Press back up to lockout.
Staying upright shifts the emphasis to the triceps; leaning forward keeps it on the chest.

exercises.name: Face-Away Bayesian Curl
instructions: Set a handle at the lowest pulley and face away from the stack, holding it with the cable running behind you.
Step forward so the arm is drawn back behind your torso with tension on the biceps.
Curl the handle up without letting the elbow drift forward, then lower to full stretch.
Having the arm behind the body puts the long head of the biceps under stretch, which a standing curl never does.

exercises.name: Preacher Hammer Curl
instructions: Set up on a preacher bench with your upper arm flat against the pad, holding a dumbbell in a neutral grip.
Curl the dumbbell up keeping the thumb pointing up throughout.
Lower to full extension under control.
The neutral grip biases the brachialis and brachioradialis while the pad prevents any shoulder contribution.

exercises.name: Cheat Curl
instructions: Load a barbell heavier than you can strictly curl and stand holding it at arm's length.
Use a controlled hip drive to get the bar past the sticking point.
Lower as slowly as you can under strict control.
The point is the overloaded lowering phase -- if the descent is not slow, the exercise has no purpose.

exercises.name: Strict Curl
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall or post, holding a barbell at arm's length.
Curl the bar up without letting your elbows travel forward or your back leave the wall.
Lower to full extension.
The wall removes every form of body english, making it the honest measure of curling strength.

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Lie face-up on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, letting the arms hang straight down beside the bench.
Curl the dumbbells up without moving the elbows.
Lower to a full stretch.
Gravity holds the arms behind the torso, loading the biceps long head in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
instructions: Attach a rope to the lowest pulley and grip an end in each hand with palms facing each other.
Curl the rope up, keeping the elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower under control to full extension.
Constant cable tension plus a neutral grip makes this a brachialis and forearm builder.

exercises.name: Katana Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Set a single handle at a high pulley and grip it with the far hand so the cable crosses your body.
Starting with the hand near the opposite shoulder, extend the arm down and across, like drawing a sword.
Return under control.
The diagonal path keeps the triceps loaded through a longer range than a straight pushdown.

exercises.name: Smith Machine JM Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench under a Smith bar with a close, shoulder-width grip.
Lower the bar towards your upper chest and throat, letting the elbows travel forward rather than flaring.
Press back to lockout using the triceps.
A hybrid of a close-grip press and a skullcrusher -- the fixed bar path makes the hybrid path repeatable.

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Kickback
instructions: Set a handle at the lowest pulley and hinge forward with your upper arm parallel to the floor.
Extend the elbow until the arm is straight, keeping the upper arm still.
Return under control.
The cable keeps tension at full lockout, which is exactly where a dumbbell kickback loses it.

exercises.name: Machine Dip
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides.
Press down until the arms are extended.
Return under control to a full stretch.
Lets you scale dip loading below bodyweight, which parallel bars cannot do without assistance.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with your hands together under your chest, index fingers and thumbs touching.
Lower your chest to your hands, keeping the elbows tucked.
Press back to full extension.
The narrow hand position shifts load from the chest onto the triceps.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and grip it with palms facing up.
Keeping your elbows at your sides, extend the arms down to lockout.
Return under control.
The supinated grip biases the medial head of the triceps.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and grip it with one hand, palm down or neutral.
Keeping the elbow pinned to your side, extend the arm to full lockout.
Return under control.
Working one arm at a time exposes and corrects side-to-side strength differences.

exercises.name: Dumbbell French Press
instructions: Sit upright holding a single dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Lower it behind your head by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms vertical.
Extend back to overhead.
The overhead position stretches the triceps long head, which pushdowns leave largely unloaded.

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip it firmly behind your head.
Drive your legs up until your body is nearly vertical, supported only on your upper back.
Lower the whole body as one rigid unit, stopping before your hips touch down.
The body must stay in one line -- bending at the hips removes almost all of the difficulty.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie on your back and press your lower back flat into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor, arms extended overhead.
Hold the position, keeping the lower back in contact with the floor throughout.
If the lower back lifts off the floor, raise the legs higher until it does not.

exercises.name: L-Sit
instructions: Support yourself on parallettes, rings, or the floor with arms locked out and shoulders depressed.
Lift your legs straight out in front so your body forms an L.
Hold, keeping the knees locked and the toes pointed.
Tucking the knees is the standard regression while building the hip flexor and ab strength to hold it straight.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel holding an ab wheel under your shoulders.
Roll forward as far as you can while keeping your lower back from arching.
Pull back to the start using your abs, not your hip flexors.
Range should be limited by how far you can go without the lower back sagging, not by how far you can reach.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your body still.
Raise your knees towards your chest, curling the pelvis up at the top.
Lower under control without swinging.
The pelvic curl at the top is what makes the abs work -- lifting the knees alone is mostly hip flexors.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
instructions: Support yourself on the arm pads of a captain's chair with your back against the pad and legs hanging.
Raise your legs until they are parallel to the floor or higher.
Lower under control.
Supporting the forearms removes grip as the limiting factor, so the abs fail before the hands do.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
instructions: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are in line with your torso.
Hold briefly, return, and alternate sides.
The hips and shoulders must stay square -- rotation means the core has stopped resisting.

exercises.name: Weighted Plank
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank and have a partner place a plate across your upper back.
Hold a straight line from head to heels, bracing the abs and squeezing the glutes.
Hold for time.
Adding load is how the plank keeps progressing once hold times run past a minute or so.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
instructions: Hold the end of a landmine-mounted barbell at chest height with both hands, arms extended.
Rotate the bar from side to side in an arc, pivoting the back foot as you go.
Control the bar through the whole arc rather than letting it swing.
Rotation should come from the hips and thoracic spine, not the lumbar.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper
instructions: Set a handle at a high pulley and stand side-on, gripping it with both hands.
Pull the handle down and across your body towards the opposite hip, pivoting the back foot.
Return under control.
Keep the arms relatively straight -- bending them turns this into a pulldown.

exercises.name: Toes to Bar
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Keeping the legs relatively straight, raise your feet up to touch the bar between your hands.
Lower under control.
Requires enough lat engagement to stop the body swinging, which is why it is harder than a hanging leg raise.

exercises.name: Seated Torso Rotation Machine
instructions: Sit in the machine with your legs secured and your torso against the pads.
Rotate your torso to one side against the resistance.
Return under control and complete the set before switching sides.
Use moderate loads and a controlled range -- loaded lumbar rotation punishes aggressive weight jumps.

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pads against your chest and grip the handles.
Crunch forward by flexing the spine, not by pulling with the arms.
Return under control without letting the stack touch down.
One of the few ways to progressively load the abs with the same precision as any other muscle.

exercises.name: Burpee
instructions: From standing, squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank and perform a push-up.
Jump the feet back under you and finish with a jump, reaching overhead.
The staple full-body conditioning movement -- pace it, since form degrades fast under fatigue.

exercises.name: Wall Ball
instructions: Hold a medicine ball at chest height and stand facing a wall.
Squat to depth, then drive up explosively and throw the ball at a target on the wall.
Catch it on the way down and flow straight into the next squat.
The catch should absorb into the next squat -- stopping between reps makes it far less effective as conditioning.

exercises.name: Ski Erg
instructions: Stand facing the machine and grip both handles overhead.
Drive the handles down past your hips by hinging at the hips and engaging the lats.
Return to the overhead position and repeat in a continuous rhythm.
Power comes from the hinge, not the arms -- pulling with the arms alone burns out quickly.

exercises.name: Assault Bike
instructions: Sit on the fan bike with the seat height set so your knee is slightly bent at full extension.
Drive with the legs while pushing and pulling the handles.
Maintain a target pace or work in intervals.
Resistance scales with effort, so it self-regulates -- the harder you push, the harder it pushes back.

exercises.name: Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a harness or hold straps connected to a loaded sled and face away from it.
Walk or run forward against the resistance, keeping a forward lean.
Maintain steady tension for the target distance.
Dragging backwards instead loads the quads heavily and is commonly used for knee rehab.

exercises.name: Man Maker
instructions: Start standing with a dumbbell in each hand, then place them down and jump back into a plank.
Perform a push-up, then a row with each arm.
Jump the feet back in, clean the dumbbells to your shoulders and press overhead.
One of the most demanding conditioning complexes there is -- keep the load light relative to your strength.

exercises.name: Devil's Press
instructions: Stand over two dumbbells and perform a burpee, bringing your chest to the floor between them.
As you stand, swing both dumbbells between your legs and up overhead in one continuous movement.
Lock out overhead, then return them to the floor.
The dumbbells travel in one unbroken arc -- pausing at the shoulders makes it a burpee to snatch instead.

exercises.name: Thruster
instructions: Hold a barbell in a front rack position with the elbows high and feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat to full depth.
Drive up out of the squat and use the momentum to press the bar to lockout overhead in one movement.
The squat and press are one continuous action -- pausing between them makes it a squat plus a press.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
instructions: Set the treadmill to a steep incline and a brisk walking pace.
Walk without holding the handrails, letting your arms swing naturally.
Maintain the pace for the target duration.
Holding the rails offloads a large share of the work and largely defeats the point of the incline.

exercises.name: Jacob's Ladder
instructions: Clip the waist belt on and grip the rungs of the angled ladder.
Climb in a continuous hand-over-hand, foot-over-foot pattern.
Speed of the ladder is set by how high you climb, so maintain your position to hold a pace.
The self-paced design makes it low-impact while still reaching very high heart rates.

exercises.name: VersaClimber
instructions: Set your feet in the pedals and grip the handles at shoulder height.
Climb using opposite arm and leg together in a vertical, cross-crawl pattern.
Keep the stride length consistent and the torso upright.
Full-body and zero-impact, which is why it is a common substitute when running volume needs cutting.

exercises.name: Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from a bar or rings with a false grip.
Pull explosively so the bar reaches your lower chest, then drive the chest forward over the bar.
Press to lockout with arms straight and the body above the bar.
The transition, not the pull, is the limiting factor -- practise it with a band or on low rings first.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand with a flat back.
Stand tall with the shoulders back and walk for the target distance or time.
Keep the torso upright and avoid leaning to one side.
Grip usually fails first -- straps turn it into a trap and core exercise rather than a grip one.
